# Transformer Attention & Scaled Dot-Product Attention

## The Intuition

In a sequence (sentence, audio frame, etc.), every element should be able to "look at" every other element and decide how much to pay attention to it. This is the core idea behind **attention**: instead of processing tokens in a fixed window or sequentially (as RNNs do), each position computes a weighted sum over *all* positions.

The three matrices that make this work:

| Matrix | Role | Analogy |
|--------|------|---------|
| **Q** (Queries) | "What am I looking for?" | A search query you type into a database |
| **K** (Keys) | "What do I contain?" | The metadata/index on each document |
| **V** (Values) | "What is the actual content?" | The body text of each document |

For every position *i*, its query **qᵢ** is compared against every key **kⱼ**. The similarity score tells position *i* how much to pull from value **vⱼ**.

## The Math: Scaled Dot-Product Attention

$$\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V$$
